source.title: DecisionLLM: Large Language Models for Long Sequence Decision Exploration
source.authors: Xiaowei Lv; Zhilin Zhang; Yijun Li; Yusen Huo; Siyuan Ju; Xuyan Li; Chunxiang Hong; Tianyu Wang; Yongcai Wang; Peng Sun; Chuan Yu; Jian Xu; Bo Zheng

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some internal inconsistencies appear in the reported numbers and data sizes; these are noted below.
record.tranche_reason: The study applies model- and data-scaling experiments to offline long-sequence decision-making and reports downstream task performance, a new setting relative to the language-model pretraining-loss claims.
record.gate_note: The study does not measure held-out cross-entropy, fit power laws to loss, test extrapolation from small runs, or find a compute-optimal parameter/token split. Its own scaling results concern decision-task returns and scores. The prompt-based representation analysis, data-quality comparisons, and pretrained-weight ablation do not measure the claim versions unless they are part of the task-performance scaling results below.
record.test_reason: It fine-tunes Qwen2.5 LLMs at 0.5B, 1.5B and 3B and varies training-set size on offline decision tasks. It reports Maze2D scores, which bear weakly on V6 in a new setting: downstream performance rising with model and data scale. It fits no scaling function and measures no pretraining loss.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors claim 'scaling laws' in model size, data volume and data quality, and say model and data scaling are linked: 3B needs more data. They also claim an SFT ceiling, approached by 1.5B on Maze2D. No law is fitted; the claims rest on monotonic trends over three sizes.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures Maze2D and AuctionNet decision-task returns and scores for fine-tuned DecisionLLM models, rather than held-out language-model pretraining loss or compute-optimal allocation. It reports no power-law fits or extrapolation tests.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance depends on dataset size: the 3B model performs poorly on the compact dataset but improves with expanded data. Performance also depends on training-data curation and collection policy, though those comparisons are not scaling-law fits.

fits_no_version.finding: A filtered 130k-sample dataset outperforms the unfiltered 800k-sample dataset on Maze2D returns. Data with exploratory noise reaches peak returns of about 220 versus about 150 without noise (1.5B).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In offline decision fine-tuning of LLMs, data quality and diversity outweigh data quantity.

record.problems: The scaling evaluation is limited to one Maze2D task and a few model sizes; the paper reports no fitted scaling function or predictive evaluation. It selects peak performance across evaluation checkpoints for comparison experiments. Results depend on data volume, and the text's 130k-to-400k data-size description conflicts with Figure 5's legend showing 13w, 26w, and 60w.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results bearing on V6 were left out. The paper's AuctionNet comparison reports only one DecisionLLM size, so it does not provide a model-scale comparison there.

untested.parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute. Only the fine-tuning MSE objective is used, and its value is not reported.
Extrapolation from small runs. No fits are made.
Compute-optimal allocation between parameters and tokens.
Architecture shape at a fixed parameter count.
Power-law form in the fine-tuning/decision regime. Only three model sizes and three data sizes are compared, with no functional fit.
Whether the improvement is predictable (a fitted law), its relation to pretraining loss, and model-size scaling on AuctionNet (only 3B was run).
Fitted exponents, fitting choices, and curvature.

missing.what: DT-extended (about 720k params, score 109.9 ± 47.29), which the authors use as the smallest point in their parameter-scaling trend
Filtered 130k vs unfiltered 800k data comparison, showing a smaller dataset performing better

record.verdict_notes: The study's 'scaling laws' are qualitative trends with large SDs. Table 1 reports each model's best result over data scales and the peak over checkpoints, which confounds model size with data size. The headline numbers are inconsistent: the abstract's 69.4-point Maze2D gain over DT does not match Table 1 (78.4). The AuctionNet gain is given as 0.085 in the abstract and 0.058 in the contributions; Table 2 gives 0.085. Dataset sizes are also inconsistent (400k vs 60w; 10M steps vs 10M trajectories).

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether power laws fitted on small runs predict much larger runs.
Fixed-compute allocation between parameters and tokens, including the growth rates of either.
Architecture-shape effects at fixed parameter count.
Power-law behavior across modalities or training regimes such as repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.

The study evaluates Maze2D and AuctionNet decision-task performance, not a broad set of downstream tasks or performance as a function of pretraining loss. It does not fit a predictive scaling function.
It reports no fitted exponents, compute-optimal split, comparison of fitting methods, or evidence about power-law curves bending away from a fit.

rows.subject: DecisionLLM(0.5B)

rows.note: This is the smallest DecisionLLM model in the reported parameter-scale comparison; the paper says Table 1 reports each model's optimal performance across data scales.

relationships.condition: Maze2D-umaze-v1, 0.5B to 1.5B, and increasing training-set size
relationships.reason: Score rises 130.86→145.16 (Table 1) and 73.06→117.76 (Table 3). The text reports monotonic gains with dataset size (r2, r5, r7, r8).
relationships.display_finding: Increasing model size from 0.5B to 1.5B raised scores 130.86→145.16 and 73.06→117.76 in the reported comparisons, while larger datasets yielded monotonic gains.

relationships.condition: Maze2D-umaze-v1, 3B, on full data and on the compact 130k dataset
relationships.reason: 3B matches 1.5B (142.26 vs 145.16, r3) and falls below it on 130k data (93.79 vs 117.76, r6). The authors cite an SFT ceiling and insufficient data.
relationships.display_finding: The 3B model performed similarly to 1.5B on full data (142.26 versus 145.16) and worse on 130k data (93.79 versus 117.76), attributed to fine-tuning saturation and insufficient data.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
